docs.title: GLEIF CLI
docs.text: A command-line tool for working with GLEIF (Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation) golden copy datasets. It downloads the three public LEI datasets, loads them into a local DuckDB database, and lets you query ownership hierarchies, search entities by name, and resolve ISINs.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Step Command What happens Download gleif download Fetches three GLEIF ZIP files from the golden copy API, extracts CSVs Load gleif load Bulk-loads the CSVs into DuckDB with column renaming Query gleif lei <LEI> Looks up parents, children, siblings, and reporting exceptions Search gleif name <QUERY> Case-insensitive substring search across 2M+ legal names Status gleif status Shows row counts and publish dates for loaded datasets

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
GLEIF publishes three "golden copy" datasets daily:

Level Dataset Contents Level 1 LEI Records (lei2) ~2.3M legal entities: names, addresses, jurisdictions, statuses Level 2 Relationships (rr) Parent-child consolidation links between entities Level 2 Reporting Exceptions (repex) Entities that cannot or do not report ownership relationships

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
# First-time setup: download and load all datasets (~5 min)
gleif refresh

# Look up Apple Inc.'s global ultimate parent and subsidiaries
gleif lei HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394

# Show the full corporate tree from any node
gleif lei HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394 --tree

# Search for entities with "Deutsche Bank" in their legal name
gleif name "Deutsche Bank"

# Check how fresh your local data is
gleif status

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
All commands are run via uv run gleif <command> (or gleif <command> if installed globally).

Usage: gleif [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  GLEIF Golden Copy data loader and LEI relationship query CLI.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  download  Download and extract all GLEIF golden copy datasets.
  load      Load extracted CSVs into DuckDB.
  lei       Look up an LEI and display all related entities.
  name      Search for entities by legal name.
  refresh   Download and load GLEIF data in one step.
  status    Show database status: record counts and data freshness.

docs.title: Global options
docs.text: Option Default Description --db PATH ~/.local/share/gleif/gleif.duckdb Path to the DuckDB database file --data-dir PATH ~/.local/share/gleif/data Directory for downloaded data files

docs.title: gleif download
docs.text:
Download and extract all three GLEIF golden copy datasets from the golden copy API.

Usage: gleif download [OPTIONS]

Options:
  --data-dir PATH  Directory for downloaded data files.
  --force          Re-download even if local data is current.
  --help           Show this message and exit.

docs.title: Freshness check
docs.text: Before downloading, the command sends a HEAD request to check the x-gleif-publish-date header. If the local publish-date marker matches the remote, the download is skipped. Pass --force to bypass this check.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
Each dataset is downloaded as a ZIP, extracted to a CSV, and the ZIP is deleted. Extracted CSV names follow the GLEIF convention:

<date>-gleif-goldencopy-lei2-full-publish.csv
<date>-gleif-goldencopy-rr-full-publish.csv
<date>-gleif-goldencopy-repex-full-publish.csv

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 All datasets downloaded successfully (or already current, skipped) Non-zero Network or HTTP error (unhandled exception)

docs.title: gleif load
docs.text:
Load already-extracted CSVs into DuckDB. Useful when CSVs are intact but you need to reload (e.g., after a schema change).

Usage: gleif load [OPTIONS]

Options:
  --db PATH        Path to the DuckDB database file.
  --data-dir PATH  Directory for downloaded data files.
  --help           Show this message and exit.

Note

If no extracted CSV is found for a dataset, the command exits with code 1 and instructs you to run gleif download first.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 All CSVs loaded successfully 1 A required CSV is missing; run gleif download first

docs.title: gleif refresh
docs.text:
Combines download and load in a single step. This is the recommended way to update your local database.

Usage: gleif refresh [OPTIONS]

Options:
  --db PATH        Path to the DuckDB database file.
  --data-dir PATH  Directory for downloaded data files.
  --force          Re-download even if local data is current.
  --help           Show this message and exit.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Download and load completed successfully Non-zero Network or HTTP error (unhandled exception)

docs.title: gleif lei
docs.text:
Look up a single LEI and display its relationship report or corporate hierarchy tree.

Usage: gleif lei [OPTIONS] LEI_CODE

Arguments:
  LEI_CODE  The LEI to look up. Must be exactly 20 characters.  [required]

Options:
  --db PATH          Path to the DuckDB database file.
  --isin             Fetch ISINs from the GLEIF REST API.
  --tree             Show full corporate hierarchy tree.
  --max-depth INT    Maximum depth for hierarchy traversal.  [default: 50]
  --help             Show this message and exit.

docs.title: Default output (flat report)
docs.text:
Without --tree, the command displays a structured report with:

  • Entity panel: LEI, legal name, status, category, jurisdiction, addresses, registration status
  • Direct Parent: The entity that directly consolidates this one (IS_DIRECTLY_CONSOLIDATED_BY)
  • Ultimate Parent: The top-level consolidating entity (IS_ULTIMATELY_CONSOLIDATED_BY)
  • Children: All entities that report this LEI as their direct or ultimate parent
  • Siblings: Entities sharing the same direct parent
  • Other Relationships: Non-consolidation relationships (branches, fund links, etc.)
  • Reporting Exceptions: Reason codes if the entity cannot report ownership data

docs.title: Tree output (--tree)
docs.text: Walks the full corporate hierarchy from the ultimate parent down to all descendants, rendered as a Rich tree. Diamond structures (entities with multiple parents) are deduplicated: the first occurrence is shown in full; later references show (see above).

docs.title: ISIN lookup (--isin)
docs.text: Fetches ISINs from the GLEIF REST API (/lei-records/{lei}/isins) for all LEIs in the report or tree. Makes additional HTTP requests; expect a few seconds of latency.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 LEI not found in database, or invalid LEI format

docs.title: gleif name
docs.text:
Search for entities by legal name using a case-insensitive substring match.

Usage: gleif name [OPTIONS] QUERY

Arguments:
  QUERY  Name or substring to search for.  [required]

Options:
  --db PATH        Path to the DuckDB database file.
  -n, --limit INT  Maximum number of results.  [default: 100]
  --isin           Fetch ISINs from the GLEIF API.
  --help           Show this message and exit.

Results are displayed in a table with columns: LEI, Legal Name, Jurisdiction, Status. Passing --isin adds an ISINs column.

gleif name "volkswagen" --limit 20

docs.title: Match behavior
docs.text: Queries use a parameterized case-insensitive substring match (ILIKE $1 with bind value %query%) against the legal_name column, using DuckDB's default collation. Results are ordered alphabetically by legal name. Passing --limit caps the result count; the default is 100.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success (results found, or no results)

docs.title: gleif status
docs.text:
Display the current state of the local DuckDB database.

Usage: gleif status [OPTIONS]

Options:
  --db PATH  Path to the DuckDB database file.
  --help     Show this message and exit.

Shows a table with dataset name, publish date, load timestamp, and row count.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Database exists and data is loaded 1 Database file not found, or no data loaded yet

docs.title: Local setup
docs.text:
# Clone and install all dependencies (runtime + dev)
git clone https://github.com/ByronWilliamsCPA/gleif.git
cd gleif
uv sync --all-extras

# Install pre-commit hooks (one-time)
uv run pre-commit install

docs.title: Running tests
docs.text:
Tests use in-memory DuckDB with CSV fixtures in tests/conftest.py. No downloaded GLEIF data is required.

# Run all tests with coverage
uv run pytest

# Single file
uv run pytest tests/test_queries.py

# Single test
uv run pytest tests/test_queries.py::TestGetEntity::test_finds_existing_entity

# Run all tests with coverage report
uv run pytest --cov-report=html

# Open the HTML report (run the one for your platform)
open htmlcov/index.html          # macOS
xdg-open htmlcov/index.html      # Linux
start htmlcov/index.html         # Windows (Git Bash only)
explorer.exe htmlcov/index.html  # WSL

docs.title: Test fixture hierarchy
docs.text:
The loaded_db fixture provides a pre-populated in-memory DuckDB with four entities:

Ultimate Parent
    └── Parent
            ├── Child A
            └── Child B

CLI tests use typer.testing.CliRunner with on-disk DuckDB files in tmp_path.

docs.title: Coverage thresholds
docs.text: Scope Threshold Line coverage 80% Branch coverage 70% Critical paths 90% New patches 90%

docs.title: Linting and type checking
docs.text:
uv run ruff format .            # Format code
uv run ruff check --fix .       # Lint and auto-fix
uv run basedpyright src         # Type check

Ruff uses the PyStrict-aligned rule set at 88-character line length. BasedPyright runs in standard mode with strict inference for lists, dicts, and sets.

docs.title: Pre-commit hooks
docs.text:
Pre-commit runs automatically on every commit. To run manually:

uv run pre-commit run --all-files
Hook Purpose trailing-whitespace Remove trailing whitespace end-of-file-fixer Ensure files end with a newline check-yaml / check-json / check-toml Validate config files detect-private-key Block accidental key commits ruff (format + lint) Python formatting and linting markdownlint Markdown style enforcement yamllint YAML style enforcement bandit Python security scanning

docs.title: Building the documentation
docs.text:
uv run mkdocs serve     # Live-reload local preview
uv run mkdocs build     # Build static site to site/
uv run mkdocs gh-deploy # Deploy to GitHub Pages

The site/ output directory is gitignored.

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text: Three GitHub Actions workflows run on every PR and push to main:

docs.title: CI (ci.yml)
docs.text:
1. Test suite with 80% coverage gate
  2. Quality checks: ruff format --check, ruff check, basedpyright
  3. CI gate that blocks merge on any failure

All action steps are pinned to commit SHAs.

docs.title: Security (security-analysis.yml)
docs.text:
Runs on PRs and weekly on a schedule (separate workflow to save ~5-8 min per PR):

  1. CodeQL static analysis
  2. Dependency review (GPL denied, known CVEs blocked)
  3. Bandit security linting
  4. OSV dependency vulnerability scanning

docs.title: Qlty (qlty.yml)
docs.text:
Triggered after CI succeeds. Uploads coverage.xml to Qlty Cloud for coverage trend tracking.

Qlty also runs locally via pre-commit: qlty fmt on pre-commit (auto-format staged files), qlty check on pre-push.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] CHANGELOG.md updated with version and date
  • [ ] All tests pass above coverage thresholds
  • [ ] No vulnerabilities older than 60 days
  • [ ] uv run pre-commit run --all-files passes cleanly
  • [ ] Version tag follows SemVer (v0.1.0, v1.0.0, etc.)
  • [ ] All release commits are GPG-signed

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or newer
  • uv (recommended) or pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/ByronWilliamsCPA/gleif.git
cd gleif

# Install with uv (installs all runtime and dev dependencies)
uv sync --all-extras

The gleif command is then available via:

uv run gleif --help

docs.title: First run
docs.text:
The datasets are large (the Level 1 LEI file alone is ~800 MB compressed). Allow 5-10 minutes for the initial download on a typical broadband connection.

Disk space

The initial refresh requires approximately 2 GB of free disk space: ~835 MB for the three ZIP archives during download, plus ~1 GB for the loaded DuckDB database. The ZIPs are deleted after extraction, leaving ~1 GB in use at steady state.

# Download all three datasets and load them into DuckDB in one step
uv run gleif refresh

Output:

Refreshing GLEIF data...
  Level 1 - LEI Records ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 100% 823 MB  4.2 MB/s
  Level 2 - Relationships ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 100%  12 MB  4.1 MB/s
  Level 2 - Reporting Exceptions ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 100%   3 MB  4.0 MB/s

Loading into ~/.local/share/gleif/gleif.duckdb...
  Loading Level 1 - LEI Records...    2,381,240 rows loaded
  Loading Level 2 - Relationships...  4,012,887 rows loaded
  Loading Level 2 - Reporting Exceptions...  521,044 rows loaded
  Creating indexes...
  Done.
Refresh complete.

docs.title: File locations
docs.text:
By default, data and the database are stored under your home directory:

Path Contents ~/.local/share/gleif/data/ Extracted CSVs and publish-date markers ~/.local/share/gleif/gleif.duckdb DuckDB database file

Override these with --data-dir and --db on any command:

uv run gleif refresh --data-dir /mnt/data/gleif --db /mnt/data/gleif.duckdb

docs.title: Keeping data fresh
docs.text:
GLEIF publishes updated golden copy files daily. Re-running gleif refresh is safe: it checks the x-gleif-publish-date response header and skips downloading if your local copy is already current.

# No-op if already up to date
uv run gleif refresh

# Force re-download regardless of freshness
uv run gleif refresh --force

Check when your data was last loaded:

uv run gleif status

docs.title: Your first LEI lookup
docs.text:
uv run gleif lei HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394

This returns a structured report with:

  • Entity details (name, status, jurisdiction, addresses)
  • Direct parent (immediate consolidating entity)
  • Ultimate parent (top of the ownership chain)
  • Children (entities that report this LEI as their parent)
  • Siblings (entities sharing the same direct parent)
  • Reporting exceptions (if the entity cannot disclose ownership)

To see the full corporate hierarchy as a tree:

uv run gleif lei HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394 --tree

To include ISIN mappings from the GLEIF REST API:

uv run gleif lei HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394 --isin

An ISIN (International Securities Identification Number) is a 12-character alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies a security such as a stock or bond. GLEIF maps LEIs to ISINs where the legal entity is also an issuer of securities.

docs.title: Known Vulnerabilities
docs.text:
No known vulnerabilities are currently tracked.

Review quarterly. No entry should age past 60 days without reassessment. By policy, vulnerabilities older than 60 days block releases; review this file before tagging any release.

Last reviewed: 2026-04-24

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: Response-Aware Development is a systematic approach to identifying and mitigating implicit assumptions in AI-generated code. This document explains the rationale, implementation, and evaluation criteria for the RAD system.

docs.title: The Hidden Assumption Crisis
docs.text:
AI coding assistants (including Claude) make implicit assumptions that:

  • Pass initial testing in development environments
  • Work correctly under ideal conditions
  • Fail catastrophically in production under load, concurrency, or edge cases

docs.title: Common Failure Patterns
docs.text:
1. Timing Assumptions: State updates assumed to complete instantly
  2. Resource Availability: External services assumed always available
  3. Data Integrity: Input validation assumed handled elsewhere
  4. Concurrency: Race conditions in async operations
  5. Type Safety: Runtime type mismatches at boundaries

docs.title: Real-World Impact
docs.text:
# This code killed production at 3 AM:
conn = get_connection()
results = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM lei_records WHERE lei = ?", [lei]).fetchall()
# Assumes connection is always valid and table is loaded - WRONG under cold start

# This code survived production:
conn = get_connection()
if conn is None or not table_exists(conn, "lei_records"):
    raise RuntimeError("Database not initialized; run 'gleif load' first")
results = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM lei_records WHERE lei = ?", [lei]).fetchall()

docs.title: Core Innovation: Context Isolation
docs.text: The key insight is that the same context that made an assumption cannot effectively review it. We need fresh eyes (a different AI context) to spot blind spots.

docs.title: Three-Tier Risk Model
docs.text:
We classify assumptions by potential impact and route them to appropriate models:

Tier Tag Risk Level Model Use case 1 #CRITICAL Production outages, data loss Opus 4.7 Multi-step decisions, deep reasoning 2 #ASSUME Functional bugs, UX issues Sonnet 4.6 Standard verification, code review 3 #EDGE Rare scenarios, optimizations Haiku 4.5 Quick lookups, structural checks

docs.title: Phase 1: Tagging (Current)
docs.text:
• Claude adds assumption tags during code generation
  • Developers can manually add tags during review
  • Tags include risk level and verification hints

docs.title: Phase 2: Verification (Automated)
docs.text:
• Slash command triggers multi-model verification
  • Parallel processing for efficiency
  • Fresh context prevents confirmation bias

docs.title: Phase 3: Remediation (Guided)
docs.text:
• Verification agent generates defensive code
  • Fixes applied automatically or via review
  • Assumptions marked as verified

docs.title: Quantitative Metrics
docs.text:
To evaluate effectiveness after 30-60 days:

  1. Assumption Detection Rate
  2. Total assumptions tagged per 1000 lines of code
  3. Distribution across risk tiers

  4. Most common assumption categories

  5. Fix Application Rate

  6. Percentage of assumptions that needed fixes
  7. Percentage of fixes applied vs deferred

  8. Time from detection to remediation

  9. Production Impact

  10. Production incidents traced to assumptions
  11. Incidents prevented by RAD fixes

  12. Mean time to resolution (MTTR) improvement

  13. Cost Efficiency

  14. Average cost per verification
  15. Percentage handled by free models
  16. ROI: incidents prevented vs verification cost

docs.title: Qualitative Metrics
docs.text:
1. Developer Experience
  2. Ease of understanding tagged assumptions
  3. Quality of generated fixes

  4. Workflow integration friction

  5. Model Performance

  6. Accuracy of risk classification
  7. Quality of fixes by model tier

  8. False positive rate

  9. Pattern Recognition

  10. Recurring assumption patterns identified
  11. Improvements to initial code generation
  12. Knowledge base growth

docs.title: Short-term (30 days)
docs.text:
• [ ] 80% of critical assumptions caught before production
  • [ ] <$0.01 average cost per file verified
  • [ ] <2 minute verification time for typical PR

docs.title: Medium-term (60 days)
docs.text:
• [ ] 50% reduction in assumption-related production incidents
  • [ ] Pattern database with >100 common assumptions
  • [ ] Automated fix rate >70% for standard assumptions

docs.title: Long-term (90+ days)
docs.text:
• [ ] Claude proactively avoids learned assumption patterns
  • [ ] Organization-specific assumption knowledge base
  • [ ] Near-zero critical assumptions reaching production

docs.title: Potential Risks and Mitigations
docs.text:
1. Over-tagging: Too many trivial assumptions
  2. Mitigation: Clear guidelines on what to tag

  3. Focus on production-impacting assumptions only

  4. Model Hallucination: Incorrect fixes from verification

  5. Mitigation: Human review for critical fixes

  6. Test coverage requirement for all fixes

  7. Performance Impact: Slow verification blocking commits

  8. Mitigation: Parallel processing

  9. Async verification for non-critical items

  10. Developer Resistance: Additional workflow complexity

  11. Mitigation: Clear value demonstration
  12. Gradual rollout starting with critical only

docs.title: Setup Requirements
docs.text:
• [ ] CLAUDE.md updated with RAD tagging standards (see global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md)
  • [ ] Team members familiar with #CRITICAL, #ASSUME, #EDGE tag semantics
  • [ ] Pre-commit hooks configured (optional)

docs.title: Verification Points
docs.text:
• [ ] Test with synthetic assumption examples
  • [ ] Verify tags are caught during code review
  • [ ] Confirm #VERIFY instructions are actionable

docs.title: Monitoring Setup
docs.text:
• [ ] Assumption tracking database/log
  • [ ] Cost monitoring dashboard
  • [ ] Incident correlation tracking
  • [ ] Developer feedback channel

docs.title: Example Workflow
docs.text:
# 1. Developer codes with Claude
$ claude "implement lei lookup with parent traversal"
# Claude generates code with #CRITICAL/#ASSUME/#EDGE tags and #VERIFY instructions

# 2. Before commit, review tagged assumptions
$ grep -rn '#CRITICAL\|#ASSUME\|#EDGE' src/
# Work through each #VERIFY instruction manually or via PR review

# 3. Commit with assumptions documented
$ git commit -m "feat: lei parent traversal with RAD assumption tags"

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Response-Aware Development represents a shift from "hope it works in production" to "verify assumptions systematically". By running multiple AI models with fresh contexts, we can catch subtle issues that single-context development misses.

The tiered approach balances quality and cost: premium models handle critical assumptions while free models cover the bulk of verification work.

Success will be measured by reduced production incidents, improved code quality, and developer confidence in AI-generated code.

Document Version: 1.1 Last Updated: 2026-05-14

docs.title: DuckDB file locked
docs.text:
Symptom: The command fails immediately with an error similar to:

duckdb.duckdb.IOException: Could not set lock on file
"~/.local/share/gleif/gleif.duckdb": Conflicting lock is held

Cause: DuckDB allows only one writer connection at a time. If a previous gleif command was interrupted without closing cleanly, or if another process (such as a DuckDB shell session or a Jupyter notebook) still has the file open, subsequent write operations will be blocked.

Fix:

  1. Identify and close the process holding the lock:

    lsof ~/.local/share/gleif/gleif.duckdb

  2. Close or kill the process, then retry the command.

Note

Read-only tools such as DB browsers can sometimes hold a shared lock that blocks writes. Close them before running gleif load or gleif refresh.

docs.title: Download timeout or partial failure
docs.text:
Symptom: The download progress bar stalls, the terminal shows a network error, or the command exits before all three datasets are downloaded:

httpx.ReadTimeout: timed out while receiving response

Cause: The Level 1 LEI file is approximately 800 MB compressed. A slow or unstable connection may time out mid-stream, leaving a partial ZIP on disk.

Fix:

Re-run the download. The freshness check compares the x-gleif-publish-date header against a local marker file; because the partial download did not write a valid marker, the command will restart the download cleanly:

uv run gleif download

To force a full re-download regardless of any existing marker:

uv run gleif download --force

Tip

Run the download on a wired connection or a machine with a stable network connection. On typical broadband (4-5 MB/s), all three datasets take 5-10 minutes.

docs.title: CSV not found (load before download)
docs.text:
Symptom: Running gleif load without having downloaded the data first produces an error and exits with code 1:

No extracted CSV found for Level 1 - LEI Records. Run 'gleif download' first.

Cause: gleif load expects the extracted CSVs to already exist in the data directory. It does not download them.

Fix:

Run gleif download (or gleif refresh, which combines both steps) before gleif load:

# Download only
uv run gleif download

# Or download + load in one step (recommended)
uv run gleif refresh

docs.title: Disk space
docs.text:
Symptom: The load command fails partway through, or the database file is unexpectedly small after loading. The error may mention disk space:

IOException: No space left on device

Cause: The fully loaded DuckDB file is approximately 1-2 GB. Combined with the extracted CSVs (roughly 900 MB in total), you need at least 3 GB of free space in the target partition during a refresh.

Check available space:

df -h ~/.local/share/gleif/

Fix:

Free up disk space, then re-run the load:

uv run gleif load

To store the database on a different partition, use --db and --data-dir:

uv run gleif refresh --data-dir /mnt/large-disk/gleif --db /mnt/large-disk/gleif.duckdb

Warning

If a gleif.duckdb file exists but the load was interrupted, the file may be in a partially written state. Delete it and reload to ensure a clean database:

rm ~/.local/share/gleif/gleif.duckdb
uv run gleif load

docs.title: Proxy and TLS issues
docs.text:
Symptom: Downloads fail with a TLS or SSL certificate error:

httpx.ConnectError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed

Cause: Corporate networks that perform TLS inspection (MITM proxies) can present a self-signed or corporate root certificate that Python's default trust store does not recognize.

Fix:

Set the SSL_CERT_FILE environment variable to point to your corporate CA bundle:

export SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/to/corporate-ca-bundle.pem
uv run gleif refresh

If your proxy requires explicit configuration, set the standard proxy environment variables before running any command:

export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.example.com:8080
uv run gleif refresh

Warning

Do not disable SSL verification entirely. Passing verify=False to httpx removes all certificate validation, which exposes the connection to man-in-the-middle attacks. Contact your network team for the correct CA bundle instead.

docs.title: Stale or missing data
docs.text:
Symptom: LEI lookups return no results, or results appear out of date relative to the GLEIF registry. There is no visible error.

Cause: GLEIF publishes updated golden copy files daily. If gleif refresh has not been run recently, the local database may be days or weeks behind the current registry.

Check data freshness:

uv run gleif status

Sample output:

 Dataset                      Publish Date   Loaded At              Rows
 Level 1 - LEI Records        2026-04-25     2026-04-26 07:31:02    2,381,240
 Level 2 - Relationships      2026-04-25     2026-04-26 07:33:15    4,012,887
 Level 2 - Reporting Exc.     2026-04-25     2026-04-26 07:34:02      521,044

Fix:

Update to the latest published data:

uv run gleif refresh

refresh checks the x-gleif-publish-date header before downloading. If your local copy is already current, it exits quickly without re-downloading.

Note

GLEIF typically publishes at approximately 08:00 UTC. Data from the current calendar day may not yet be available if you run gleif refresh shortly after midnight UTC.

docs.title: Database does not exist yet
docs.text:
The behavior differs depending on which command you run:

gleif status on a missing database: The command checks whether the database file exists and exits immediately with:

Database not found at <path>. Run 'gleif refresh' first.

gleif lei / gleif name on a missing or empty database: These commands do not check for the database file before connecting. duckdb.connect() silently creates an empty file if none exists, so queries return empty results rather than an error. gleif lei reports the LEI as not found, and gleif name returns an empty results list.

Fix:

Run the initial load before querying:

uv run gleif refresh

See Getting Started for full first-run instructions.

docs.title: Data pipeline
docs.text:
GLEIF REST API
    │
    │  HEAD  x-gleif-publish-date (freshness check)
    │  GET   /golden-copies/publishes/{dataset}/latest.csv  (streamed ZIP)
    ▼
download.py ──► extract CSV from ZIP ──► delete ZIP
    │
    │  DownloadResult (csv_path, publish_date, dataset_type)
    ▼
db.py ──► DuckDB read_csv() with column select/rename
    │
    │  CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ... AS SELECT <column_map> FROM read_csv(...)
    ▼
DuckDB file at ~/.local/share/gleif/gleif.duckdb
    │
    │  parameterized SQL queries
    ▼
queries.py ──► frozen dataclasses (models.py)
    │
    ▼
cli.py ──► Rich terminal output (panels, tables, trees)

docs.title: Module map
docs.text: Module Responsibility constants.py Dataset URLs, CSV-to-DB column mappings, DatasetType enum, relationship type constants download.py Async download of three GLEIF ZIP files with freshness checking via publish-date markers; DownloadResult dataclass db.py DuckDB connection management, CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE via read_csv(), index creation, load metadata tracking queries.py LEI lookup functions: entity info, parent traversal, children, siblings, reporting exceptions, corporate group tree models.py Frozen dataclasses: EntityInfo, RelatedEntity, ReportingException, HierarchyNode, CorporateGroup, LEIRelationshipReport isin.py ISIN lookup via GLEIF REST API (/lei-records/{lei}/isins); single and batch with httpx cli.py Typer app with all commands; Rich rendering of reports, tables, and hierarchy trees

docs.title: DuckDB as the local store
docs.text:
The GLEIF golden copy datasets are large (Level 1 is ~2.3M rows with 338 columns). DuckDB's read_csv() function can bulk-load these files in seconds using parallel I/O. Queries run against the local file without any server process, which keeps the tool self-contained.

The full Level 1 CSV has 338 columns. Loading only the ~30 relevant columns via a SELECT inside read_csv() avoids storing data that is never queried and keeps the database file small.

docs.title: Relationship direction convention
docs.text:
In the GLEIF relationship dataset, start_node_id is the child and end_node_id is the parent. This follows the GLEIF spec: the relationship type is IS_DIRECTLY_CONSOLIDATED_BY, read left-to-right as "child IS_DIRECTLY_CONSOLIDATED_BY parent".

-- Find the direct parent of an entity
SELECT end_node_id AS parent_lei
FROM relationships
WHERE start_node_id = '<child_lei>'
  AND relationship_type = 'IS_DIRECTLY_CONSOLIDATED_BY'
  AND relationship_status = 'ACTIVE'

-- Find all children of an entity
SELECT start_node_id AS child_lei
FROM relationships
WHERE end_node_id = '<parent_lei>'
  AND relationship_type = 'IS_DIRECTLY_CONSOLIDATED_BY'
  AND relationship_status = 'ACTIVE'

docs.title: Cycle prevention in recursive queries
docs.text:
Corporate ownership structures can contain cycles (e.g., cross-holdings). Both get_ancestor_chain and get_descendant_tree use DuckDB's recursive CTE with a path array to track visited nodes and halt if a cycle is detected:

WHERE NOT list_contains(a.path, r.end_node_id)

The MAX_HIERARCHY_DEPTH constant (default: 50) provides a secondary depth limit.

docs.title: Async download with sequential loading
docs.text: All three datasets are downloaded concurrently using asyncio.gather() with a shared Rich progress bar. Loading is done sequentially: DuckDB connections are not thread-safe, and CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE DDL statements cannot be parallelized over a single connection.

docs.title: Frozen dataclasses as query return types
docs.text: All query results are returned as frozen dataclasses (@dataclass(frozen=True)). This prevents accidental mutation of results between query and render, and makes the types hashable for use in sets and dict keys (e.g., deduplicating LEI lists for batch ISIN lookups).

docs.title: Python data model
docs.text:
Query functions in queries.py return frozen dataclasses from models.py:

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EntityInfo:
    lei: str
    legal_name: str
    entity_status: str
    registration_status: str
    entity_category: str | None
    legal_jurisdiction: str | None
    legal_address_city: str | None
    legal_address_country: str | None
    hq_address_city: str | None
    hq_address_country: str | None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RelatedEntity:
    lei: str
    legal_name: str | None
    relationship_type: str
    relationship_status: str
    direction: str  # "parent" | "child" | "sibling" | "other"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReportingException:
    exception_category: str
    exception_reason: str | None
    exception_reference: str | None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HierarchyNode:
    lei: str
    legal_name: str | None
    depth: int  # 0 = starting entity, 1 = parent, etc.
    entity_status: str | None
    entity_category: str | None
    legal_jurisdiction: str | None
    relationship_type: str | None
    parent_lei: str | None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CorporateGroup:
    root: EntityInfo
    descendants: list[HierarchyNode]
    total_entities: int

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LEIRelationshipReport:
    entity: EntityInfo
    direct_parent: EntityInfo | None
    ultimate_parent: EntityInfo | None
    children: list[RelatedEntity]
    siblings: list[RelatedEntity]
    other_relationships: list[RelatedEntity]
    reporting_exceptions: list[ReportingException]

docs.title: Session Summary
docs.text:
Metric Value Repos reviewed 1 (ByronWilliamsCPA/gleif) Total findings (net of overrides) 49 Critical 10 Important 22 Suggested 13 Unclassified candidates 8 Findings remediated 45 Findings requiring manual action 4

All 49 findings from 7 domain agents were approved for remediation (option B: all critical + important + suggested). Four findings could not be auto-remediated and require deliberate user action outside the CLI.

docs.title: Patterns Observed
docs.text:
• OpenSSF required files absent: All five of LICENSE, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, and README.md (empty) were missing or empty. This is the most common first-run failure pattern for repos that were bootstrapped from a minimal template without a compliance pass. Appeared in 5 of 5 required-file checks (5/5 checks failing).

  • Mutable tags in pre-commit config: All 5 rev values in .pre-commit-config.yaml were mutable tags rather than SHA pins. This is a supply-chain risk that is easy to miss because pre-commit does not warn on mutable revs at install time.

  • Bandit || true in CI: The security scan step in ci.yml appended || true, causing all Bandit findings to be silently swallowed. CI showed green while the scanner found real issues. This pattern provides false assurance and is worth a dedicated manifest check.

  • Unpinned action SHAs in CI: Two actions (qltysh/qlty-action/coverage@v2 and qltysh/qlty-action@v2) used mutable version tags. This mirrors the pre-commit mutable-tag pattern at the GitHub Actions layer.

  • BasedPyright in standard mode: The project had BasedPyright configured in standard mode rather than strict. The toolchain-auditor found this important enough to remediate; strict mode surfaces a class of type errors that standard mode hides.

  • Missing harden-runner in CI jobs: Three jobs (detect-changes, security-gate, ci-gate) lacked step-security/harden-runner, leaving those jobs without network egress monitoring.

  • CLAUDE.md missing required sections: Model Selection, RAD, and Compact Instructions sections were all absent from the project CLAUDE.md. These are required by the global standard but are easy to omit when CLAUDE.md is authored before the global standard is finalised.

  • Em-dashes in documentation: 19 em-dash characters were found across CLAUDE.md and docs/index.md. This violates the hard rule in the global writing standard and was not caught earlier because pre-commit did not yet enforce it. The no-em-dash pre-commit hook was added as part of remediation.

  • Branch protection absent: Branch protection was not configured on main. This is a common pattern for solo-maintainer repos where the developer is the only committer and treats the protection as an unnecessary friction. The OSSF Scorecard penalises this regardless of team size.

  • Scorecard workflow absent: No .github/workflows/scorecard.yml existed, meaning the repo was invisible to OpenSSF Scorecard automated scoring.

docs.title: FOUND-005b: Empty README at project root
docs.text:
Projects using MkDocs or similar doc generators often treat docs/index.md as the primary entry point and leave README.md empty or with a one-line placeholder. GitHub visitors see a blank repository description. Proposed check:

- id: FOUND-005b
  domain: foundations
  severity: critical
  description: "README.md is present but empty or contains only a placeholder (< 50 non-whitespace characters)"
  verify: "file_min_content: README.md, 50"
  override_eligible: false
  notes: "Distinct from FOUND-005 (absent). Catches repos that pass file_exists but provide no content."

docs.title: CI-007a: Security scanner silenced with || true
docs.text:
Appending || true to a SAST or dependency scanner in CI causes the job to pass even when the scanner finds real issues. The scanner is present but provides false assurance. Proposed check:

- id: CI-007a
  domain: ci
  severity: important
  description: "Security scanner step in CI uses '|| true' or equivalent, silencing all findings"
  verify: "grep_absent: .github/workflows/*.yml, '|| true'"
  override_eligible: false
  notes: >
    Covers Bandit, osv-scanner, pip-audit, and similar tools. Acceptable alternative:
    scope the scanner to --level HIGH so only high-severity findings block CI, but do
    not suppress the exit code entirely.

docs.title: CI-HARDEN-001: harden-runner absent from non-build jobs
docs.text:
Jobs that do not build artifacts (gates, detection jobs, notification jobs) are commonly missed when harden-runner is added because authors focus on the jobs that actually run code. Proposed check:

- id: CI-HARDEN-001
  domain: ci
  severity: important
  description: "One or more CI jobs are missing step-security/harden-runner as the first step"
  verify: "all_jobs_have_step: .github/workflows/*.yml, step-security/harden-runner"
  override_eligible: true
  notes: >
    Jobs that use 'runs-on: ubuntu-latest' or any GitHub-hosted runner should include
    harden-runner. Override is eligible for jobs that run in a fully isolated
    self-hosted environment with network egress already controlled at the infra level.

docs.title: ARCH-001: Module-level Rich Console in library code
docs.text:
Projects that start as scripts and are later refactored into importable libraries often retain module-level Console() instances that emit output when library functions are called. This breaks the library contract (callers cannot suppress output) and interferes with test capture. Proposed check:

- id: ARCH-001
  domain: architecture
  severity: suggested
  description: "Library module instantiates Rich Console() or print() at module level, coupling import to side effects"
  verify: "grep_absent: src/**/*.py, '^console = Console()'"
  override_eligible: true
  notes: >
    Acceptable pattern: pass a Console instance as a parameter or use a module-level
    logger instead. Override eligible for intentional CLI-only entry-point modules
    (e.g., cli.py) where the module is never imported by other library code.

docs.title: Agent Scope Expansion Candidates
docs.text:
• python-toolchain-auditor: Currently checks for [tool.interrogate] presence only. Consider adding a check for fail-under threshold value; projects that add the section but set fail-under=0 (or omit it, accepting the default of 0) satisfy the presence check while gaining no enforcement. A threshold of 70 or higher should be required.

  • pre-commit-auditor: Currently checks for the presence of a no-em-dash hook but does not verify the regex pattern used. A hook that matches the em-dash character (U+2014) but not -- (double hyphen used as a substitute) would pass the presence check while missing a common variant. Consider verifying the pattern string, not just hook presence.

  • devops-deployment-agent: The || true pattern (CI-007a above) is not currently in scope. The agent checks for scanner presence but not for exit-code suppression. Expanding to grep for || true adjacent to known scanner invocations would catch this class of false-assurance findings.

  • ossf-compliance-auditor: The solo-maintainer branch-protection pattern warrants a note in the check. When required_approving_review_count cannot be set to 1 because there is only one maintainer, the correct remedy is to enable branch protection with a bypass rule for the maintainer, not to skip protection entirely. The auditor's remediation guidance should distinguish between "absent entirely" and "present but zero reviews required."

docs.title: High-Frequency Existing Checks
docs.text:
The following checks failed in this session. Because only one repo was reviewed, frequency is expressed as pass/fail rather than a percentage. All of these are candidates for prioritised remediation in any new repo that enters the compliance pipeline.

Check ID Description Status FOUND-001 SECURITY.md absent FAILED - remediated FOUND-002 CONTRIBUTING.md absent FAILED - remediated FOUND-003 CHANGELOG.md absent FAILED - remediated FOUND-004 LICENSE absent FAILED - remediated FOUND-005 README.md empty FAILED - remediated PC-012 Pre-commit revs are mutable tags FAILED - remediated TOOL-006 Ruff rule codes missing from select FAILED - remediated TOOL-007 BasedPyright not in strict mode FAILED - remediated PC-003 basedpyright pre-commit hook absent FAILED - remediated PC-005 detect-secrets hook absent FAILED - remediated PC-011 no-em-dash hook absent FAILED - remediated CI-006 Unpinned action SHA in CI FAILED - remediated CI-006b harden-runner missing from 3 jobs FAILED - remediated OSSF-004 Branch protection absent FAILED - manual action required OSSF-005 Dependabot absent FAILED - remediated

docs.title: Manual Action Items (not auto-remediable)
docs.text:
These items were identified but could not be remediated programmatically. They require deliberate user action and should be tracked as follow-on work.

  1. Branch protection on main (OSSF-004): Enable via gh api or the GitHub UI. The remediation command was provided during the session. For a solo-maintainer repo, enable protection with a maintainer bypass rule so force-push to main is still possible when needed. Required before OSSF-009 (PR review enforcement) can be addressed.

  2. Private Vulnerability Reporting (OSSF-002 partial): The GitHub API rejected the enable request because the repository is private. This feature is available on public repos and GitHub Enterprise. The SECURITY.md file was created with a contact email fallback. No further action needed unless the repo is made public or migrated to GitHub Enterprise.

  3. Best Practices Badge (OSSF-001-BADGE, SCORECARD:CII-Best-Practices): Requires manual registration at bestpractices.coreinfrastructure.org. No API pathway exists for automated registration. Once registered, the badge URL should be added to README.md.

  4. Signed releases and SBOM (SCORECARD:Signed-Releases, SCORECARD:SBOM): Both are now addressed by the release.yml workflow added in this PR. It uses Sigstore keyless signing and anchore/sbom-action for SPDX SBOM generation on tagged releases. The Scorecard workflow will pick up the change automatically.

docs.title: Follow-on Technical Work
docs.text:
The following items were identified during remediation but deferred. They represent real gaps, not cosmetic issues.

  1. Ruff violation cleanup (20 new violations from TOOL-006): Adding 13 Ruff rule codes surfaced 20 new violations: TC001/TC002/TC003 (TYPE_CHECKING import guards), S608 (SQL in string literals, likely false positives in queries.py that use parameterised queries), and ASYNC240 in download.py. Each category requires a targeted fix: import guards for TC*, inline # noqa: S608 with a tracking comment for confirmed false-positive SQL strings, and an httpx-compatible async pattern for ASYNC240.

  2. Test coverage gaps: download.py has no unit tests. The CLI commands load, refresh, and download are also untested. Coverage gates currently pass because the covered modules pull the aggregate above 80%, but these modules represent the data pipeline entry points and carry the highest operational risk.

  3. fetch_isins_batch docstring: The docstring for this function describes incorrect parameter semantics. This was flagged by the darglint hook after it was added. Should be fixed as part of the Ruff cleanup pass.

  4. load CLI command importing private functions: The load command imports functions that are named with a leading underscore, indicating they are not part of the public API of their module. This should be resolved either by making the functions public or by restructuring the module boundary.

  5. gleif name empty string guard: Passing an empty string to the name command produces a query that matches all records. A guard clause or a minimum-length validator on the Typer argument should be added.
